sources.title: EcoStruxure IT Expert — official DCIM product overview
sources.actual_read: HTML substantive lines9–62 and FAQ153–158; page total193lines, via web open, not search-only.
supports: One vendor DCIM example centralizes visibility for power/cooling/IT assets, device/environment alarms, reports and analysis.
Some software management capabilities include device discovery/configuration, user management and remote firmware deployment.
does_not_support: Universal DCIM scope or a complete DCIM standard definition.
Actual site discovery, sensors, points, alarm values, polling interval/latency, connection state, installation or autonomous control.
All devices support remote firmware/configuration or every DCIM deployment supports identical write actions.
sources.adopted_limit: Only generic monitoring/alarms/analysis/management role and conditional optional operations. No AI, downtime prevention, sustainability/UPS health or real-time performance claims are adopted.

sources.title: Johnson Controls — Data Center Building Controls
sources.actual_read: HTML substantive lines312–393; page total516lines. Read monitoring/control at322, system description337, access/logs363, software monitor/command/report376, distributed controller381 and sensor-data collection393.
supports: One BMS/BAS example includes environmental/connected-equipment monitoring, software commands and reporting; local controllers and sensors are separate from supervisory software.
Actual BMS offerings can include equipment control and automated response, with access-control/event-log capabilities.
does_not_support: That a generic DCIM screen directly closes a plant loop or bypasses local controllers/protection.
Specific setpoints, controller algorithms, failover/redundancy, PUE/WUE values, safety/compliance, site topology or installed controllers/sensors.
sources.adopted_limit: Represent supervisory environmental/equipment role; if local control is referenced, use a separate conditional functional boundary, no new physical ID or unmodeled actuator geometry. Automation may exist in particular designs, but TA28 does not certify it.

sources.title: Power Monitoring Expert 2024 — Default User Access Level Privileges
sources.actual_read: Full substantive HTML table lines27–115, page total122; original official URL redirects to canonical. Original/reference open returned actual text twice. One direct canonical re-open returned tool-access error, retained as failed read attempt, then reference re-open succeeded.
supports: This power-monitoring software distinguishes application viewing, alarm acknowledgment, dashboard/trend/report work and configuration through permissions.
Alarm acknowledgment and view permissions differ; user-group application scope is an additional condition.
Device connection/configuration, UPS/generator configuration, Modbus gateway and notifications are separate gated functions in this example.
does_not_support: That acknowledging an alarm fixes its physical cause, or that reading telemetry authorizes a device write.
A universal five-role system, an installed EPMS, all electric metrics/quality analysis, automatic breaker operation, point mapping or local control readiness.
sources.adopted_limit: Use electricity-focused monitoring/alarms/trends/reports as a functional lane; optional operations require product capability, integration and software permission. Do not label software credentials as six site rights.

scope: Actual independent primary text read, generic software responsibilities only; not site implementation or verified reference pixels
